displayName: Oracle Health Millennium / Cerner-Grounded Hospital Response Reference Profile

vendorSemantics.note: Oracle Health Millennium provides SMART/FHIR context plus Message Center PERSONNEL/GROUPINBOX recipients, responsible personnel and HIGH(STAT)/NORMAL(ROUTINE) message priority. Clinical severity bands, activation criteria, response teams and escalation timing are hospital-configured. Public MU Health Care evidence shows a Cerner Rapid Response implementation using Low/Moderate/High/Very High NEWS categories and a hospital nursing protocol; these are not universal Oracle/Cerner levels.

evidenceRules.reason: Pulseless/cardiac-arrest evidence requires immediate code/emergency response activation.
Ventricular fibrillation is an immediately life-threatening arrest rhythm and requires code/emergency response activation.
Critical deterioration meets the reference profile's rapid-response activation floor unless stronger arrest/resuscitation evidence requires code response.
Hypotension is a common rapid-response activation criterion in hospital deterioration pathways.
Low MAP indicates hemodynamic deterioration requiring rapid-response-level assessment in this reference profile.
Marked tachycardia requires urgent provider review; concurrent instability may independently raise the pathway to rapid response.
Marked bradycardia requires urgent provider review; concurrent instability may independently raise the pathway.
Significant hypoxemia meets the reference profile's rapid-response activation floor.
Marked hyperkalemia requires urgent provider evaluation; ECG/hemodynamic instability may raise the response pathway.
Marked hypokalemia requires urgent provider evaluation.
Elevated digoxin concentration requires urgent provider review.
Marked lactate elevation with deterioration warrants rapid-response-level assessment in this reference profile.

responseTierProfile.claimBoundary: T0/T1/T2/T3/E are CARDINAL normalized response tiers, not official Oracle/Cerner product levels.

publicImplementationPattern.organization: University of Missouri Health System / MU Health Care
publicImplementationPattern.solution: Cerner Rapid Response Solution with NEWS/PEWS
publicImplementationPattern.documentedOperationalPattern: High/Very High notifications; automatic Rapid Response based on NEWS severity or provider unable to reach bedside within 15 minutes.
publicImplementationPattern.mappingNote: CARDINAL uses T0/T1/T2/T3 as a portable policy interface qualitatively aligned to low/moderate/high/very-high response intensity. It does not claim to reproduce MU NEWS thresholds.

MU_PROVIDER_BEDSIDE_15_MINUTES.appliesTo: T2_URGENT_REVIEW -> T3_RAPID_RESPONSE only when adopted by site policy
MU_PROVIDER_BEDSIDE_15_MINUTES.note: Public MU Health Care implementation reported Rapid Response notification when a provider was unable to be at bedside within 15 minutes after nursing notification. Do not apply this universally.
